title: PRE 17 — Test
src: Isolation of the Operating Field — Rubber Dam (1)

mcqs.q: Moisture control in operative dentistry means excluding:
opts: Sulcular fluid, saliva and gingival bleeding from the field
mcqs.explain: Moisture control refers to excluding sulcular fluid, saliva and gingival bleeding from the operating field.

mcqs.q: The RECOMMENDED technique for moisture control is the:
mcqs.explain: Although suction and absorbents help, the rubber dam is generally the recommended technique for moisture control.

mcqs.q: Who first described the rubber dam, and when?
mcqs.explain: S.C. Barnum first described the rubber dam in 1864.

mcqs.q: The use of a rubber dam is considered mandatory in:
mcqs.explain: Rubber dam use is mandatory in restorative and endodontic procedures, for isolation and protection.

mcqs.q: An ADVANTAGE of the rubber dam is:
opts: A dry, clean operating field with improved visibility
mcqs.explain: Advantages include a dry/clean field, improved visibility, improved material properties, protection and efficiency.

mcqs.q: The rubber dam protects the patient by:
opts: Preventing aspiration/swallowing of instruments and debris
mcqs.explain: By covering the throat, the dam protects the patient (and operator) from aspiration or swallowing of small instruments/debris.

mcqs.q: Why does the rubber dam improve dental-material properties?
opts: It prevents moisture/saliva contamination during placement
mcqs.explain: A dry, contamination-free field lets materials (e.g. bonding/composite) set with their optimal properties.

mcqs.q: A DISADVANTAGE of the rubber dam is that it is:
opts: Time-consuming and may meet patient objection
mcqs.explain: Disadvantages include being time-consuming, possible patient objection, difficulty on unusual teeth, and asthma/latex issues.

mcqs.q: Which situation makes clamp placement difficult?
opts: Partially erupted teeth, third molars or malpositioned teeth
mcqs.explain: Unusual tooth shapes/positions — partially erupted teeth, third molars, malpositioned teeth — cause inadequate clamp placement.

mcqs.q: A patient with bronchial asthma may not tolerate the rubber dam because:
mcqs.explain: Asthmatic patients who find nasal breathing difficult may not tolerate the dam covering the mouth.

mcqs.q: For a patient allergic to latex, the rubber dam:
opts: Can be replaced with a latex-free dam
Must never be used in any form
mcqs.explain: Latex allergy is a contraindication for latex dams, but latex-free dams can be used instead.

mcqs.q: Which is a PART of the rubber-dam armamentarium?
opts: Sheet, holder/frame, clamp, punch, forceps and napkin
mcqs.explain: Parts include the rubber dam sheet, holder/frame, clamp (retainer), punch, retainer forceps, napkin and accessories.

mcqs.q: The rubber dam sheet is usually made of:
mcqs.explain: Rubber dam sheets are made of natural latex rubber; latex-free versions exist for allergic patients.

mcqs.q: Common rubber-dam sheet sizes are:
mcqs.explain: Rubber dam sheets come in 5×5 inch and 6×6 inch sizes.

mcqs.q: Rubber dam material should be reasonably new because old material:
opts: Deteriorates and has low tear strength
mcqs.explain: Like all rubber, the dam deteriorates over time, giving low tear strength, so fresh material should be used.

mcqs.q: The Young's frame is:
opts: A U-shaped frame with projections that secure and stretch the dam
mcqs.explain: The Young frame is a U-shaped metal/plastic frame with small projections that secure and stretch the borders of the dam.

mcqs.q: The function of the rubber-dam holder/frame is to:
opts: Support and stretch the edges of the dam
Anchor the dam to the tooth
mcqs.explain: The holder/frame supports the edges of the dam (keeping it stretched and away from the field).

mcqs.q: A rubber-dam clamp (retainer) consists of:
opts: Four prongs and two jaws joined by a bow
A single jaw and a handle
mcqs.explain: The clamp has four prongs and two jaws connected by a bow.

mcqs.q: The PRIMARY function of the rubber-dam clamp is to:
mcqs.explain: The clamp's primary function is to anchor/stabilise the dam on the anchor tooth (and it also helps retract gingiva).

mcqs.q: The rubber-dam PUNCH is used to:
opts: Cut holes of different sizes for different teeth
mcqs.explain: The punch cuts holes of different sizes (selected per tooth) in the dam sheet.

mcqs.q: The retainer (clamp) forceps are used to:
mcqs.explain: The retainer forceps engage the clamp's forceps holes to place and remove the clamp.

mcqs.q: If a clamp is accidentally dropped, the rubber dam helps by:
opts: Preventing it from being aspirated or swallowed
mcqs.explain: Because the dam covers the oropharynx, a dropped clamp/instrument is caught, preventing aspiration or swallowing.

saqs.q: Define moisture control and name the recommended method.
saqs.a: Excluding sulcular fluid, saliva and gingival bleeding from the field; recommended method = the rubber dam.

saqs.q: List four advantages of the rubber dam.
saqs.a: Dry/clean field, improved visibility, improved material properties, patient/operator protection (and efficiency).

saqs.q: List the disadvantages/contraindications of the rubber dam.
saqs.a: Time-consuming, patient objection, unusual tooth positions (partial eruption, third molars), asthma, latex allergy.

saqs.q: Name the parts of the rubber-dam system.
saqs.a: Sheet, holder/frame, clamp (retainer), punch, retainer forceps, napkin (+ accessories).

saqs.q: Describe the rubber-dam sheet (material and sizes).
saqs.a: Natural latex (latex-free available); sizes 5×5 and 6×6 inch; use fresh material (loses tear strength).

saqs.q: Describe the rubber-dam clamp and its function.
saqs.a: 4 prongs + 2 jaws joined by a bow; it anchors/stabilises the dam and retracts gingiva.

saqs.q: What do the punch and retainer forceps do?
saqs.a: The punch cuts holes (sized per tooth); the forceps place/remove the clamp.
